<div class="proj-section">
  <h2 class="proj-section__title">About the project</h2>
  <p>PriceBeo is a mobile app that lets users scan any product barcode in-store and instantly compare prices across Ireland's five major retailers: Tesco, Dunnes Stores, Lidl, Aldi, and SuperValu. With grocery prices up 27% since 2021 and limited tools available to Irish shoppers, the app targets a clear and validated market gap.</p>
  <p>As CTO, my role was to lead the technical vision and strategy for the platform. This meant understanding how the technology worked, making informed decisions about architecture and data infrastructure, and working closely with outsourced developers and technical advisors to bring the product to life. I bridged the gap between the business team and the technical side, ensuring our solution was feasible, well-structured, and clearly communicated.</p>
</div>

## Financial projections

The chart below visualises PriceBeo's three-year financial model, comparing projected revenue against startup and operating costs across the growth period.

```{python}
#| label: fig-financials
#| fig-cap: "PriceBeo — projected revenue vs costs over three years"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

years = ["Year 1", "Year 2", "Year 3"]
revenue = [99_440, 312_500, 938_625]
startup = [157_720, 0, 0]
operating = [60_000, 98_000, 210_000]

x = np.arange(len(years))
width = 0.28

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
b1 = ax.bar(x - width, revenue, width, label="Revenue (€)", color="#4a90d9", alpha=0.9)
b2 = ax.bar(x, startup, width, label="Startup Costs (€)", color="#e67e22", alpha=0.9)
b3 = ax.bar(x + width, operating, width, label="Operating Costs (€)", color="#e74c3c", alpha=0.9)

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(years)
ax.set_ylabel("Amount (€)")
ax.set_title("PriceBeo — 3-Year Financial Projections", fontweight="bold")
ax.legend()
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"€{int(v):,}"))
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

for bar in [*b1, *b2, *b3]:
    h = bar.get_height()
    if h > 0:
        ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, h + 4000,
                f"€{int(h):,}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.5)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
